Brand colour almost never ships at 100%
Every brand guideline specifies colour at full strength. In a dashboard
that colour spends its life at 60%, 30%, 10% — fills, ramps, banding,
disabled states. The guideline says nothing about those. That's where
I was checking tints one at a time on

There is no single label colour that is safe
— so any dashboard that sets one
label colour for a whole chart family is failing somewhere
on that ramp. That's not a judgement call, it's arithmetic,
and it's the sort of thing worth having a machine check.

text.tspan: Verified tints export as SVG straight back into Figma — into the design
system, not a screenshot folder. The audit stopped being a final step
and became part of the definition of done.
AI-assisted development got me to "working" in an evening.
, and a tool that audits accessibility
has to earn the second. The first version was fast, confident and wrong
— and nothing in the interface said so.
I'm a designer, not an engineer. The lesson isn't to stop building tools.
It's that building them obliges me to know what my artefacts claim on
